what’s got into you? phrase

also what’s come over you?, what’s the matter with you?, are you out of your mind?, what are you raving about?, what possessed you?

classical

Plaut. Epid. 475b: Quae tē intemperiae tenent?
Plaut. Aul. 71: nesciō pol quae illunc hominem intemperiae tenent

Quae tē intemperiae tenent?

what storm has got hold of you? what madness is this?

(vōx cōmica: Plaut.)

Intemperiae is properly foul weather; in comedy, a fit of madness (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Quae tē intemperiae tenent?

    What’s got into you?Plaut. Epid. 475b

  • nesciō pol quae illunc hominem intemperiae tenent

    I really don’t know what has got into the manPlaut. Aul. 71

See also be mad, what’s the matter?, crazy.

SourcesLewis & Short: intemperiae

Plautus, Aulularia 71; Epidicus 475b.
